newsitem.title: USA: Retailers expected to report spending cooled in April.
newsitem.headline: Retailers expected to report spending cooled in April.

text.p: Consumers took a breather in April after a three-month shopping spree and the slowdown in sales probably pinched first-quarter earnings at some major store chains, industry analysts said Tuesday.

Apparel retailers, department stores and discount chains are due to report April sales results on Thursday, and analysts said sales rose only modestly or edged lower last month after rising at a faster clip earlier in the year.
A cold snap and heavy rain in some parts of country cooled consumer spending on spring clothing, gardening tools and other seasonal goods, the analysts said.
"Sales were soft for a lot of April," said Patrick McCormack of Alex. Brown & Sons Inc. in New York. "I think the first quarter will prove to be pretty good, not gangbusters."
Alex. Brown estimated sales at major chains rose 3.5 percent in April, down from the 4.1 percent rise in March, but up from 1.3 percent in April 1996.

Kmart Corp., the nation's third-largest retailer, said on Monday that sales were "slightly negative" last month. Kmart, along with other retailers, will report monthly sales on Thursday and first-quarter profits later this month.
In a statement, Kmart Chairman Floyd Hall said April was disappointing partly because promotions for Easter took place in March.
Kmart sales at stores open at least a year, known as same-store sales, jumped 12.7 percent in March, but analysts expected the company to report a decline of 1 percent to 2 percent for April.

"Sales were very good in February and March," said Daniel Barry of Merrill Lynch. He predicted that Wall Street would begin "shaving" first-quarter profit estimates after April sales results were reported.

Analysts said same-store sales at Wal-Mart Stores Inc., the nation's largest retailer, rose 4 percent last month, off from a 7.2 percent rise in March, and that sales grew 2 percent or so at No. 2 Sears, Roebuck & Co. after a 1 percent March gain.
Shoppers apparently had their fill after spending freely in the first three months of the year, analysts said.

"We believe that warmer-than-normal weather in February, early tax refunds and large bonus payments were factors that stimulated sales earlier this year," Michael Conn of Gruntal & Co. said in a research report.

A few apparel chains were a hit with consumers who took to new apparel lines and sales at those stores were strong, analysts said. AnnTaylor Stores Corp. was expected to post a sales increase of about 5 percent and Intimate Brands Inc. posted about a 6 percent gain, analysts estimated.
Teen apparel stores have scored big sales gains with young shoppers who have shed "grunge" styles and stocked up on brighter and lighter clothes.

Maria O'Shea of Alex. Brown predicted companies like Claire's Stores Inc., Hot Topic Inc. and Gadzooks Inc. saw sales gains of about 6 percent last month, or twice that of chains catering to non-teens.
